rationale: The Latin anchors *emendatio* (correction/amendment), *reparatio* (repair/restoration), and *oblatio* (offering/atonement) point strongly to the broader sense of correcting a fault or wrong, rather than strictly a monetary payment. While *compensatio* and the legal attestations (L. Ethb., L. Alf. pol.) do involve financial compensation, BÓT encompasses penitential and moral remedy as well, making the general "act of correcting an error or fault" sense (redress.n.02) a better fit than the narrowly monetary damages.n.01.
